MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  SEPTEMBER 12, 2017

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZERUNYAN at 6:30 p.m. and the City Council convened into Closed Session in the
City Manager’s Office, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates.

City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis

14.  CLOSED SESSION (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER)

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - PENDING LITIGATION
  (Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a))
  Merryweather Properties v. City of Rolling Hills Estates, Cal Water
  Los Angeles County Superior Court - Case No. YC071487

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

B.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Significant exposure to litigation under Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2):
  two cases

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

  ***

  At 7:00 p.m., the COUNCIL reconvened in open session in the City Council Chamber,
  4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, CA.

  ***

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
SEPTEMBER 12, 2017
 PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ led the audience in the Pledge of Allegiance.

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR’S FREE RESIDENTIAL REFUSE
  SERVICE

  Representatives from Waste Management were present to conduct the quarterly Waste
  Management drawing for one year’s free residential refuse service. The winning entry
  was 26732 Rolling Hills Road.

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF AUGUST 8, 2017

  COUNCIL MEMBER  MITCHELL  moved,  seconded  by  COUNCIL  MEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN.

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF AUGUST 8, 2017 AS
  PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – AUGUST AND SEPTEMBER

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  APPROVED WARRANTS 58891 THROUGH 58931 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $201,742.32; SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 080117 THROUGH 080917;
  080317 (VOID); 58625; 58754 THROUGH 58758; 58796 THROUGH 58811;
  58799 (VOID); 58812 THROUGH 58887 IN THE AMOUNT OF $406,659.73 FOR
  A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $608,402.05 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR: The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to
  approve with the majority consent of the City Council. There will be no separate
  discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call
  vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER  MITCHELL  moved,  seconded  by  COUNCIL  MEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN.

  TO APPROVE ITEMS A-E.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 12, 2017
 A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the
  City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by
  title only.

  APPROVED

B.  JULY 2017 SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

C.  JULY 2017 MONTHLY REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  AUTHORITY TO DESTROY ORIGINAL DAMAGED RECORDS

  APPROVED.

E.  BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS FY 2016-17 AND 2017-18

  APPROVED.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

7.  AUDIENCE  ITEMS  NOT  ON  THE  AGENDA/WRITTEN  AND  ORAL
  COMMUNICATIONS

  NONE

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

  NONE

9.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF AUGUST 21, 2017

  COUNCIL MEMBER  ZUCKERMAN  moved,  seconded  by  COUNCIL  MEMBER
  MITCHELL.

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES
  OF AUGUST 21, 2017.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 12, 2017
 B.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF AUGUST
  21, 2017 – PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE EVENT MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council enter into an agreement with Pagaentry
  Productions to provide Parade Management Services for the Peninsula Holiday Parade
  of Lights on December 2, 2017.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT WITH PAGAENTRY
  PRODUCTIONS TO PROVIDE PARADE MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR THE
  PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE OF LIGHTS ON DECEMBER 2, 2017.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

C.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF JULY 31, 2017

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  MINUTES OF JULY 31, 2017.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

D.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF JULY
  31, 2017 – DROUGHT UPDATE AND CITY RESPONSE

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2407 modifying the
  City’s water conservation level form Level 2 to Level 1.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Assistant to the City Manager Davis
  stated that the City is still bound by the State restrictions and will continue to
  implement the water conservation efforts previously adopted.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ commented that it would be a good idea to educate
  residents to the fact that many of the City’s restrictions are still in place so that they
  understand why the medians are not being watered.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2407 MODIFYING  THE  CITY’S  WATER
  CONSERVATION LEVEL FROM LEVEL 2 TO LEVEL 1.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Manager Prichard read Resolution No. 2407 by title only.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 12, 2017
 E.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF JULY
  31, 2017 – ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING STATION USAGE FEE

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2408 approving a fee
  structure for public usage of the electric vehicle charging station in the amount of
  $0.18/kWh +$0.50 per session with a maximum time limit of three (3) hours per
  session.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2408 APPROVING A FEE STRUCTURE FOR
  PUBLIC USAGE OF THE ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING STATION IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $0.18/KWH +$0.50 PER SESSION WITH A MAXIMUM TIME LIMIT
  OF THREE (3) HOURS PER SESSION.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Manager Prichard read Resolution No. 2408 by title only.

F.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 19-17 – BLUEPRINCE SOFTWARE AGREEMENT FOR
  PLANNING AND CODE ENFORCEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve Planning Application PA-19-17,
  entering into an agreement between the City of Rolling Hills Estates and N. Harris
  Corporation (BluePrince Software), in the amount of $32,540, all to the satisfaction of
  the City Attorney

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN regarding the ongoing costs of using
  the software, Planning Director Wahba commented that the City will own and have
  access to all of the data in the system and staff will review the annual usage cost to
  ensure that the program remains cost effect.
  Also in response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Administrative Services
  Director Whitehead commented that staff will review the process for exporting the data
  to ensure that the City has access to the data in the event that BluePrince goes out of
  business.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ expressed concern regarding one of the terms in the
  agreement under data management whereby the vendor wants the City to agree to the
  allow them to host the data in a separate database, to use that data for commercial
  purposes and to have rights over the data. City Attorney Davis commented the he too
  shares concern over that point and would need to review it further along with the
  other terms he is reviewing.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN also expressed concern regarding the issue surrounding
  ownership of the data. He commented that there is no reason they should own the

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
SEPTEMBER 12, 2017
   information. He further expressed concern regarding commercial usage of the City’s
  data.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ also questioned whether or not the City would receive
  technical support for the contractor bundle portion of the program because the
  agreement is not clear. She also questioned why the cost increases annually because
  it should theoretically go down because less support is necessary.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN suggested that staff contact the City of Palo Alto as a resource for
  information about this type of technology.

  COUNCIL MEMBER  ZUCKERMAN  moved,  seconded  by  COUNCIL  MEMBER
  MITCHELL

  TO DEFER CONSIDERATION OF THIS ITEM TO A FUTURE MEETING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  PROPOSAL FROM WILLDAN ENGINEERING TO PROVIDE ENGINEERING SERVICES
  FOR STORM DRAIN REHABILITATION

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve a professional services agreement
  with Willdan Engineering to provide engineering services for Storm Drain
  Rehabilitation in the amount of $79,788

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Assistant City Manager Grammer
  noted that due to Willdan Engineering’s extensive experience with the City’s storm
  drains having prepared the inventory and conditional assessment prioritization plan,
  staff recommends retaining Willdan for this project.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO APPROVE A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH WILLDAN
  ENGINEERING TO PROVIDE ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR STORM DRAIN
  REHABILITATION IN THE AMOUNT OF $79,788.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

B.  CITY HALL AND CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER REDESIGN AND UPGRADE PROJECT

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL.

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE REPORT

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
SEPTEMBER 12, 2017
 11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

  NONE

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:  This item provides the
  opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to other
  Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of currently
  active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide governmental
  associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and their various
  committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or have an interest, which
  are not otherwise agendized.

A.  ADOPTION OF MISSION, VISION, VALUES STATEMENTS

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN suggested that a statement be added to the Vision
  Statement to make reference to the City’s operational and financial efficiencies.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN commented that the City also has many collaborative
  relationships through the contract city model, including relationships with the
  Sheriff’s Department, Fire Dept., Public Works and the City Attorney’s office.

  After a brief discussion, it was the concurrence of the City Council to add the following
  statement to the Vision Statement: Operational efficiencies through the contracting
  services model.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE MISSION, VISION VALUES STATEMENTS AS AMENDED TO
  ADD A STATEMENT REGARDING OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCIES TO THE
  VISION STATEMENT.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

B.  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL reported that the South Bay Cities Council of
  Governments (SBCCOG) is working on establishing a regional fiber optic network and
  suggested having a study session on this topic to determine how this would impact the
  City and what options the City may have.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ suggested including other technologies in the study
  session in order to look at all of the various options. Administrative Services Director
  Whitehead commented that he could put together an agenda and provide the City
  Council with an overview of this topic.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF commented that the SBCCOG recently received $90,000 from
  LA County Supervisors Janice Hahn and Mark Ridley-Thomas to help further this
  effort.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
SEPTEMBER 12, 2017
   After a brief discussion it was the concurrence of the City Council to direct staff to
  schedule a study session to provide the City Council with more information on this
  topic.

C.  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ reported that she and MAYOR ZERUNYAN met with the
  Equestrian Committee to discuss the Waste Management contract negotiations. She
  also reminded the public that there will be a community meeting on September 19,
  2017 to further discuss this topic and encouraged public participation in the process.

D.  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN reported that there are two add-on bills before the
  State legislature that could put the Community Choice Aggregation (CCA) in jeopardy.
  City Manager Prichard noted that Council Member Zuckerman will be speaking about
  CCA at the Contract Cities City Mangers group meeting in early October.

13.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS: This item provides the opportunity for Members of the
  City Council to request information on currently pending projects and/or issues of public
  concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration and/or make
  announcements of interest to the public.

A.  MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that several member of the City Council and staff will be
  attending the League of California Cities Annual Conference in Sacramento September
  13-15, 2017.

15.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 7:57 p.m. MAYOR ZERUNYAN formally adjourned the City Council meeting in
  memory of Doreen Houle co-operator the Peter Weber Equestrian Center and valiant
  supporter of the equestrian character of the community to an adjourned meeting of
  the City Council scheduled for Monday, September 18, 2017 at 4:00 p.m.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Douglas R. Prichard
City Clerk  City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  8
SEPTEMBER 12, 2017
